### Application timeline (deadlines)

Students should apply to the CO-OP program at least one year before their intended
co-op start date. The application step is in July for the Summer + Fall track or
February for the Spring + Summer track.

The process follows one of two tracks depending on the intake — **Summer + Fall**
or **Spring + Summer** — with the same steps offset by roughly five months.

**Student steps**

| Step | Action | Summer + Fall | Spring + Summer |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Apply to the co-op program | Jul | Feb |
| 2 | Meet your co-op Academic Advisor during advising week | Aug | Mar |
| 3 | Complete the co-op career development modules | Sep | Apr |
| 4 | Apply to advertised co-op positions via the CDC | Oct | May |
| 5 | Receive an offer | Dec | Jul |
| 6 | Sign the Co-op Joint Agreement Form | Jan | Aug |
| → | **Start of the co-op experience** | Jun | Jan |

### Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE)

- The standard minimum for a single approved placement is 8 full weeks, typically 320 work hours. Six company weeks alone are insufficient. ### 6+2 arrangement definition

**Question/topic:** How does a six-week internship plus two-week research arrangement work?

**Answer:** The six company weeks and two faculty-research weeks (2 weeks of research with an MSFEA faculty member) must be approved and documented. Dar Al-Handasah is an example of a company offering six-week placements, not the only company eligible for a department-approved arrangement.

## Approved Experience internship and CO-OP comparison

The department's Approved Experience internship is a graduation requirement. It
requires at least **8 weeks** of approved training and can be unpaid (see the
Summer Training Guidelines). MSFEA
CO-OP is an optional, full-time paid work term of at least **6 months**. Students
who pass FEAA 500 are no longer required to take their department's Approved
Experience / Professional Training course. The CO-OP rules and substitution are
specified in this handbook; the internship minimum comes from the Summer Training
Guidelines.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > MSFEA CO-OP (Cooperative Education) Handbook > Information for students > The FEAA 500 course]
Topic: MSFEA CO-OP (Cooperative Education) Handbook > Information for students > The FEAA 500 course
### The FEAA 500 course

A student who accepts an offer enrolls in **FEAA 500 in both semesters** of the
co-op position (Summer and Fall, or Spring and Summer):

- **First semester:** register **FEAA 500** (3 credits) and pay its tuition.
- **Second semester:** register **FEAA 500A** (3 credits) with **no additional tuition** (no additional tuition fees).

Full-time student status is maintained in both semesters. A student with
satisfactory performance at the end of the first co-op semester receives a grade
of **"In Progress (PR)"** on FEAA 500; the final **Pass or Fail** grade is
assigned on **FEAA 500A** at the end of the second semester.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > Policies]
## Policies

- **Optional or required:** CO-OP is an **optional program**, open to
  undergraduate students (and to graduate students if allowed by their
  department).
- **Hours and salary:** students work **paid full-time jobs**, a minimum of 35–40
  hours per week. Pay should be higher than a stipend but slightly below a
  fresh-graduate salary. MSFEA can provide salary guidelines, but the salary is
  set by the employer.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > Policies]
## Policies
- **Courses while on co-op:** enrolling in other courses during a co-op is **not
  allowed**, with a possible exception for a Final Year Project (FYP) or
  research-based course (499) if the department allows it and the co-op academic
  advisor (and FYP group members, for an FYP) approve — and only if it does not
  interfere with working hours.
- **Number of credits:** the co-op is a **3-credit Pass/Fail FEAA 500** course.
  Whether it counts toward academic credit, and whether it is treated as a free
  elective or a technical elective, is decided by each department. Students keep
  **full-time student status** during the co-op.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > Policies]
## Policies
- **Tuition / co-op fees:** regular tuition is charged for the 3 credits of FEAA
  500.
- **Approved Experience substitution:** students who pass FEAA 500 are **no longer
  required** to take the Approved Experience / Professional Training course in

  in the approved internship course clarification, separately from CO-OP tuition.

Your EECE 500 Final Training Report must meet these requirements:

- Length: Between 5 and 20 pages, and at least 1,500 words, excluding the cover page, references, and appendix.
- Formatting: Double spacing, size 12 font, page numbers, proper margins and indentation, and labeled figures, tables, and pictures.
- Due date: Submit it on Moodle within one week after completing your internship. If you are completing a 6+2 arrangement, submit a separate research report as well.
- Content: Follow the structure, template, and rubric on Moodle without omitting core sections. Discuss technical and administrative activities, engineering or computing projects, applications of engineering, science, and mathematics to complex problems, societal and environmental impacts, and concrete examples of acquiring and applying new knowledge. Write in your own words, cite external sources, and avoid disclosing confidential company material.

### The FEAA 500 course

A student who accepts an offer enrolls in **FEAA 500 in both semesters** of the
co-op position (Summer and Fall, or Spring and Summer):

- **First semester:** register **FEAA 500** (3 credits) and pay its tuition.

satisfactory performance at the end of the first co-op semester receives a grade
of **"In Progress (PR)"** on FEAA 500; the final **Pass or Fail** grade is
assigned on **FEAA 500A** at the end of the second semester.
